openProject:
            A button with a folder icon. It reads "Open Project…" until a
            project is open, then the project's name. Until a project is open,
            its tooltip says to pick a piton.config.pi file, whose folder
            becomes the project; once one is, the tooltip gives the project's
            path and says the button opens a different piton.config.pi.

            Clicking it opens the @{ProjectDirectoryScope} picker, and the
            folder of the file picked becomes the project. Cancelling the picker
            changes nothing, and a picker that fails shows its error as a
            notification.

            
        The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the
        application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

    shape: {RibbonShape}

        A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab
        component with its default styling. Its tabs are, in order: Project,
        Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on
        Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups.
        There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

content.text:
The Project tab's button now always reads "Open Project…". The open project's name sits at the left end of the ribbon's tab bar, before the Project tab. I haven't looked at it in the running app.

- **The name:** a small folder icon then the project folder's name, with a thin divider before the first tab. Hovering shows the full path. It's only a label, so clicking does nothing.
- **Without a project:** it reads "No project" in muted text.
- **Long names:** anything wider than 320px is cut off with an ellipsis, so the tabs don't get pushed along.
- **Collapsed ribbon:** the tabs aren't shown, so the name leads the row of small buttons instead, with the same divider after it.
- **Button tooltip:** it always says to pick a `piton.config.pi`. The path moved to the name's tooltip.

**Tests:** the ribbon test now checks that the name sits at the left end of the tab bar and comes before every button in the collapsed row.
